Personality: Luichan is a quintessential Battanian nobleman in whose veins flows the proud blood of ancient clans. Renowned for his integrity and generosity, he values honor as his very life and disdains underhanded plotting. Because his temperament lacks cold calculation, he tends to act on instinct and passion, endearing him to his subordinates even if it sometimes leaves him looking overly straightforward in complex political maneuvering. As a twenty-five-year-old commander, he much prefers settling matters with sword and spear on the battlefield to trading verbal barbs in the council hall. Sincere toward allies and open-handed toward his subjects, he is a deeply beloved young chieftain. Though known neither for extreme mercy nor reckless bravado, his oath-keeping nature and devotion to tradition have made him a respected moral standard-bearer among the Battanian nobility, upholding his clan's dignity with noble bearing.
Background: Luichan hails from the prominent Battanian house of fen Penraic and shouldered the burden of clan leadership at a young age. Holding court in the prosperous city of Seonon and governing the strategic stronghold of Flintolg Castle, his clan wields immense influence within the kingdom. Under High King Caladog's rule, Luichan has maintained steadfast loyalty; although Battanian chieftains have historically harbored strong independent streaks, he understands how vital it is to stand united beneath the banner of the sacred mountain while surrounded by the Empire and foreign foes. Trained rigorously in combat since boyhood, he is proficient with one-handed swords, polearms, and the bow, ranking among the finest of the highland warriors. As the leader of a tier-five clan, he must not only guard the pastures and fields left by his ancestors, but also lead the warriors of fen Penraic in Caladog's campaigns to defend Battania's ancient freedom, working alongside his wife Ebir to sustain the glory of his ancient house.
